claim: Hand-built story generators (TALE-SPIN) get coherence from a simulated goal stack and world model; its failures were each fixed by adding a rule or fact, and looping was stopped by not re-pushing a goal already on the stack and marking failed goals.
agent_test: Give the agent an explicit goal stack for story tasks with a code-enforced no-repeat-goal rule; compare coherence ratings against plain prompting at equal tokens.

claim: MINSTREL-style creative recall (transform-recall-adapt, TRAMs) over a small library produces many results but mostly nonsense; better indexing cuts search failure (19% to 3.5%, 58 to 16 TRAMs tried), so cost and quality depend on the library and search, not on the transform step alone.
agent_test: Run analogue retrieval from a solved-problem library with and without a typed filter on a creative task; count sensible fraction at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Harmon and Jhala Table 1 credits weighted TRAM searching and a modified boredom algorithm (Skald), not 'indexing' as such; Tearse 2011 baseline had only 35.2% sensible results.

claim: Early joke systems (JAPE) produced riddles that human judges rated low (mean 1.5 over 188 jokes) with large judge disagreement, and some outputs duplicated known jokes.
agent_test: Do not use a model as sole judge of humour; compare code-checked duplicate detection plus human ratings.

claim: ChatGPT (3.5) joke output collapses to a handful of jokes: 909 of 1008 samples matched one of 25 jokes (917 counted in another passage), top four over 50%. Gap search 2026: with 2025 frontier models (Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, GPT-4.1) direct joke prompts still give diversity 17 to 30 vs 60 to 67 with verbalized sampling (Zhang 2025); 70+ models show within-prompt similarity above 0.8 and cross-model 0.71 to 0.82 (Jiang 2025). The exact 25-joke count was not re-run on new models.
agent_test: Sample N jokes from our agent and report the count of distinct outputs; test whether prompt variation or code-side dedup raises distinctness at equal tokens.

claim: LLM output is more homogeneous than human output at population level in creative tasks (cosine variability 0.459 vs 0.738 on AUT), co-writing with InstructGPT lowers content diversity, and a Sui Generis score separates stories by novelty. Individual-level originality is close to humans. Gap search 2026: randomised designs confirm it. Doshi and Hauser: novelty +6.7%, but similarity to each other rises (b=0.87, p<0.001). Anderson 2024: group homogenisation d=0.47, individual level not significant. Min-p decoding does not fix it (61.2% of pairs above 0.8).
agent_test: Measure diversity across 20 independent attempts per prompt; test code-based diversity selection against random pick at equal tokens.

claim: On humour, LLMs trail skilled humans in several tests: caption crowd preference for Claude-3-Opus over human top-10 is 34-35% (crowd) and 1.6% (a former New Yorker editor); best multimodal model 62% vs humans 94% on caption matching; LLM-edited humorous headlines and LLM puns were rated less funny than Onion headlines and human puns. In a creative-writing benchmark humour was the lowest-scoring item (mean 3.4/10 over all models, humans also low), though the best models (Claude, Bing, GPT-4) matched human writers there. Baseline matters: against lay writers ChatGPT 3.5 jokes were funnier (2.63 vs 2.20 of 6; 69.5% preferred); against The Onion headlines no significant difference (2.37 vs 2.49, p=.14).
agent_test: Not an agent-schema test; use as a warning that humour tasks need an external human or reference check.
audit_note: Numbers check out (Zhang 34%/35.4% crowd vs 1.6% expert; Hessel 62% vs 94%; Gorenz 2.63 vs 2.20, 69.5%, 2.37 vs 2.49 p=.14), but Horvitz tested LLM headlines edited to add humour against Onion headlines (not 'edited-unfunny' ones), and the 3.4/10 humour mean in Gomez-Rodriguez is the average over all models, where Claude, Bing and GPT-4 scored on par with human writers, so it does not show LLMs trailing skilled humans.
claim_before_audit: On humour, LLMs trail skilled humans: caption crowd preference for Claude-3-Opus over human top-10 is 34-35% (crowd) and 1.6% (a former New Yorker editor); best multimodal model 62% vs humans 94% on caption matching; LLM puns and edited-unfunny headlines rated less funny than human ones; humour was the lowest-scoring item in a creative-writing benchmark (mean 3.4/10). Gap search: baseline matters. Against lay writers ChatGPT 3.5 jokes were funnier (2.63 vs 2.20 of 6; 69.5% preferred); against The Onion headlines no significant difference (2.37 vs 2.49, p=.14).

claim: Using an LLM as judge of creativity is unreliable and inconsistent: judge correlations with experts near zero (48 stories) and GPT-4 judge 54.4% win rate for Claude-3-Opus conflicts with human 35.4% and 1.6%. Contrary: GPT-4 judge pairwise accuracy 67% vs crowd 61%, and tournament judges agree with each other (Kendall tau 0.889). Gap search: judges can pass 0.5 in some settings. Agents' Room LLM judge rho 0.62 by system but 0.41 by item; zero-shot visual-creativity judges r .57 to .68 (images) and .29 to .68 (sketches); a decoupled evidence-then-score judge (CreaEval) beats direct judging; judges lose agreement on similar-quality pairs and on items where humans disagree (Jiang 2025).
agent_test: Score ideas with a model judge and a code-run or human check; report rank correlation. Keep selection in code where possible.

claim: Whether LLM stories beat human stories depends on the rater and baseline: professional New Yorker stories pass 84.7% of Torrance-based tests vs 8.7-30% for LLMs (3 to 10 times less likely, 10 expert raters, 48 stories), but a rubric scored by students found GPT-4 significantly above human students (p=0.00031) and no gap for Claude and Bing.
agent_test: Evaluate our agent on a fixed expert rubric with blind raters and report against a skilled-human baseline, not student writing.

claim: LLM stories lack human narrative structure: climax and setback turning points appear in 14.6% and 9.3% of human stories vs 1.3% and 1.7% in GPT-4 (440 narratives, 16 annotators); arc-aware prompting raised diversity about 45% and suspense or engagement about 40%.
agent_test: Add an explicit plot-arc plan (turning points) to a story task and test against plain prompting at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit structure or planning scaffolds improve LLM long-form story and comedy output in automatic and human ratings: Re3 (coherent 60.0 vs 45.7%, relevant 64.0 vs 44.0%), arc-aware prompting, COMIC agent (win rate 0.44 vs 0.30 no-refine), StoryWriter, Agents' Room. Length alone is not the driver (0.51 preference). Gap search: Agents' Room writing agents preferred by writer-annotators (9,900 ratings) but human stories still best; CritiCS plan critique wins on Interesting 85.0 vs 57.6. No study at equal tokens with blind expert raters and a skilled-human baseline was found, so the equal-token part stays untested.
agent_test: Compare plan-then-write with critique loop against plain long generation at equal tokens, human-rated; count setup cost.

claim: Non-expert readers cannot tell LLM poems from famous human poems (46.6% accuracy, 1,634 participants in study 1, 16,340 judgments) and rate AI poems higher when unlabelled; AI-labelled poems rated lower. Contrary: expert story raters and authorship tests attribute over 80% to AI for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. Gap search: the same lay-rater result holds for images and music. General users are near chance on human vs AI art (professional artists 75.3%), and Suno songs are at chance (0.53) in random pairs, 0.66 in similar pairs.
agent_test: Use blind expert plus non-expert panels; do not treat lay indistinguishability as quality.

claim: Human-AI co-writing: professionals find LLM output surprising (92% of 13 respondents) and helpful but report low ownership, plagiarism and bias concerns, and stock comedy ('1950s cruise ship material'). Small samples.
agent_test: Background only; no agent test.

claim: Training on structured thought leaps for humour (CLoT/Oogiri) improved scores by 4.3 to 10.4 points and 4.55 and 5.91 points vs LLaMA3-70B and GPT-4o, while plain chain-of-thought did not help on Oogiri.
agent_test: Train-time result, outside our no-training scope; test only whether a short leap-prompt beats plain at equal tokens.

claim: The classic symbolic systems (EMI, AARON, MINSTREL, TALE-SPIN) have almost no controlled human evaluation; EMI's chance-level audience result is stated without N and is known only through secondary sources, so the historic claims of success are weak evidence.
agent_test: None; use as a methods warning.

claim: A prompt that asks for a distribution of outputs (verbalized sampling) raises diversity 1.6 to 2.1 times in poems, stories and jokes, and human raters agree (diversity 2.39 vs 1.90 poem, 3.06 vs 2.74 story, 3.01 vs 1.83 joke, 90 lay annotators). Jokes keep quality; stories lose about 5 to 7 rubric points.
agent_test: Compare k independent attempts vs one verbalized-distribution call at equal tokens; score novelty by embedding distance and quality by a code or expert check.

claim: Different frontier models are about as alike as one model is to itself: cross-model similarity 0.71 to 0.82, so using several models as an ensemble gives little independent variety. Min-p decoding leaves 61.2% of pairs above 0.8.
agent_test: Do not count model swaps as independent attempts; measure pairwise embedding similarity of candidates and drop near-duplicates in code.

claim: Model ideas help weak writers and hurt population diversity: Doshi and Hauser (293 writers, 600 raters) novelty +6.7% with one idea, +8.1% with five; high-creativity writers did not gain; Anderson (33 participants) shows group-level homogenisation only.
agent_test: When our agent shows itself prior candidates, check whether later candidates move toward them; add a rule to propose a different frame, not a variation.

claim: Human-vs-AI detection by lay people is near chance for images (general users only slightly above a coin flip; professional artists 75.3% accuracy) and for Suno music in random pairs (0.53), and rises when pairs are matched (0.66 similar pairs). Rater expertise and matched baselines decide the result.
agent_test: Not an agent-schema test; any creative evaluation of our agent needs expert raters and matched pairs.
audit_note: Minor: Sarmento et al. 2024 is about symbolic progressive-metal music, not images or Suno, so it does not bear on the stated numbers; Ha et al. (59.2% general users, 75.32% professional artists) and Figueiredo (0.53 random, 0.66 similar, Suno) verify them.

claim: Whether a creativity judge reaches r above 0.5 depends on setting: yes zero-shot for image creativity (r .57 to .68) and for system-level story rankings (rho 0.62), no per-item for stories (0.41) or for multi-step tasks with a direct judge (PCC 0.31); two-stage evidence-then-score judging lifts multi-step agreement (QWK 0.64).
agent_test: Use a judge to rank methods across many items, not to pick one best draft; for selection use a two-stage evidence-then-score check and a code-side check.

claim: EMI audience-test evidence beyond Wikipedia was not found: only an unquantified statement that Hofstadter's audience could not beat chance; no N or counts. Ariza (2009) is the likely primary review and was not opened.
agent_test: Background only.
